summary:
Farmova AI is an AI-assisted agricultural decision-support platform that helps smallholder farmers make better-informed farming and crop-rotation decisions. Initially focused on Ghana, it turns complex Earth-observation data into practical, understandable insights.

The platform combines farm location and boundary information, environmental indicators, crop history and agricultural knowledge with NASA resources, including NASA POWER (meteorological data), GPM IMERG (precipitation estimates), SMAP (soil-moisture observations) and NASA GIBS (satellite imagery), alongside other relevant datasets.

By analysing environmental conditions alongside previous crops and locally relevant agricultural principles, Farmova AI helps farmers compare crop-rotation options and understand the reasoning behind each recommendation. Geospatial visualisation and AI-assisted explanations make this intelligence more accessible.

Ultimately, Farmova AI connects space-based science with real-world farming challenges, empowering agricultural communities to make sustainable, informed decisions.
details:
Farmova AI – Smarter Farming. Stronger Futures.

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Farmova AI is an AI-assisted agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make informed farming and crop-rotation decisions using Earth-observation data, farm information and agricultural intelligence.

The platform connects a farmer's geographical location and farm boundaries with relevant environmental information obtained from NASA Earth-observation resources. These resources provide information about rainfall patterns, temperature, soil-moisture conditions, vegetation and other environmental factors that influence agricultural activities.

Farmers can provide information about their farms, including previous crops, intended crops and farming priorities. Farmova AI brings these inputs together with environmental indicators and agricultural knowledge to support the comparison of potential crop-rotation strategies.

Its approach follows a process of farm registration, geographical identification, environmental data retrieval, data processing, agricultural analysis and understandable presentation of results. AI-assisted explanations help make complex environmental information easier for farmers to understand.

The platform is designed around the agricultural realities of Ghana, with the potential to serve farming communities across Africa.

2. What benefits does it have?

Farmova AI aims to make agricultural intelligence more accessible and useful, particularly for smallholder farmers who may have limited access to advanced agricultural information and technical resources.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Better-informed farming decisions: Helps farmers consider environmental conditions and crop history when planning their agricultural activities.
  • Environmental awareness: Makes satellite-derived rainfall, temperature, soil-moisture and vegetation information easier to understand.
  • Improved crop-rotation planning: Supports comparisons of crop-rotation options using agricultural principles and relevant environmental indicators.
  • Geographical farm intelligence: Uses GPS and farm-boundary mapping to connect environmental observations with specific farming locations while respecting dataset resolution limitations.
  • Accessible technology: Aims to simplify complex scientific information through an understandable interface and AI-assisted explanations.
  • Support for agricultural professionals: Provides a foundation for agricultural extension officers and agronomists to explore environmental information alongside farm records.

3. What is the intended impact?

Farmova AI aims to bridge the gap between space-based environmental science and everyday agricultural decision-making.

Its initial focus is Ghana, where smallholder farmers are an important part of the agricultural sector. The project seeks to make valuable environmental information more accessible to farmers who may not otherwise have the tools or technical expertise to interpret satellite-derived observations.

In the longer term, Farmova AI aims to support more informed agricultural planning, encourage responsible crop-rotation practices and strengthen the use of Earth-observation technology in African agriculture.

The platform also has potential applications for agricultural organisations, researchers, extension officers and development programmes interested in environmental monitoring and agricultural decision support.

Our long-term vision is to make advanced agricultural intelligence accessible beyond geographical and technical barriers, beginning in Ghana and expanding across Africa.

4. What tools, programming languages and software were used?

Farmova AI combines web development, geospatial technology, cloud services and Earth-observation resources.

Development environment and AI

  • Google AI Studio – primary development environment.
  • Google Gemini – AI-assisted development and conversational intelligence where implemented.

Frontend development

  • HTML5 – application structure.
  • CSS3 – interface styling and responsive layouts.
  • JavaScript – application functionality and API communication.

Backend and database

  • Supabase – backend services and authentication.
  • PostgreSQL – structured data storage.
  • PostGIS – geographical data storage and spatial operations.
  • Supabase Edge Functions – server-side API communication.

Geospatial visualisation and data presentation

  • Leaflet.js – interactive maps and farm-location visualisation.
  • Chart.js – environmental data visualisation.

NASA Earth-observation resources

  • NASA POWER – meteorological and environmental information.
  • NASA GPM IMERG – precipitation estimates.
  • NASA SMAP – soil-moisture observations.
  • NASA GIBS – satellite imagery visualisation.
  • Landsat Collection 2 – land observation.
  • NASA MODIS – vegetation and environmental observations.
  • NASA ECOSTRESS – land-surface temperature and evapotranspiration information.

Additional NASA datasets, including GRACE/GRACE-FO and GEDI, have been considered for broader environmental analysis.

File-based scientific data processing can use Python and appropriate geospatial and scientific libraries where implemented.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

Farmova AI's innovation lies in connecting multiple sources of environmental intelligence with farm-specific information and agricultural knowledge to address a practical farming challenge.

Satellite observations are often presented as complex scientific measurements that require technical expertise to interpret. Farmova AI aims to transform these observations into understandable environmental indicators that can support agricultural decisions.

Rather than treating rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and vegetation as isolated measurements, the platform considers how different environmental conditions relate to crop planning and crop-rotation choices.

Another important aspect is its combination of geospatial farm identification, environmental analysis and AI-assisted explanations. This creates an approach that connects Earth observation with practical agricultural decision support.

The project is also designed with African farming conditions in mind, particularly the needs of smallholder farmers who require accessible, understandable and locally relevant agricultural technology.

6. What factors did our team consider?

During the development of Farmova AI, we considered several important technical, environmental and social factors:

Agricultural relevance: Recommendations must consider previous crops, crop families, farming priorities and locally relevant agricultural knowledge.

Data accuracy: NASA datasets have different spatial resolutions, temporal coverage and limitations. Satellite estimates must not be presented as direct ground measurements.

Geographical precision: Farm GPS coordinates and boundaries must be handled appropriately, especially when working with satellite products whose resolution is larger than an individual farm.

Scientific reliability: Environmental observations must be processed responsibly, with consideration for missing data, quality indicators, uncertainty and data freshness.

Accessibility: The platform should be understandable to farmers with different levels of digital literacy and technical experience.

Scalability: The system should have the potential to expand beyond Ghana to other African agricultural regions.

Responsible AI: AI-generated explanations must be grounded in available environmental information and validated agricultural knowledge rather than fabricated measurements or unsupported recommendations.

Practical impact: The ultimate objective is not simply to display satellite data, but to make environmental intelligence useful for real agricultural decisions.

Conclusion

Farmova AI represents an effort to bring space-based environmental intelligence closer to the people who depend on agriculture. By connecting Earth-observation resources, geospatial technology, artificial intelligence and agricultural knowledge, the project seeks to make informed farming decisions more accessible, practical and understandable.

Farmova AI – Smarter Farming. Stronger Futures.
